answer: Five jurors sign one answer, and a split beyond one dissent slashes every signer of a divergent copy. Each unverified claim an identity files lowers its effective quorum, so a thin history needs more signatures for the same bar. Each submission carries a fresh nonce, stopping a juror from applying an old verdict to a new claim. The nadir is an honest juror on a bad connection who diverges over a format detail and loses the stake; the knoll of safety is narrower than it looks. A farm must field five real jurors per claim, so the pigment it needs, real signatures, gets expensive at scale.
